segment.description: Horse Creek, a Greene County Cherokee National Forest tributary running out of the Bald Mountains down to the Nolichucky River; TWRA spring-stocked with a special trout regulation on its national-forest reach.
segment.boundaries: Special trout regulation reach (live-verified on the state's regs publisher): 'Horse Creek: Greene County, U.S. Forest Service Boundary Line upstream to the junction of Squibb Creek.' Stocking workbook rows are undivided 'Horse Creek' (Greene County). Stocking-identity pin: the 2026-09-17 workbook contains NO 'Camp Creek' row for Greene County (its only Camp Creek entry is 'Puncheon Camp Creek', Grainger County) - all 8 weekly rows name 'Horse Creek', so the catalog reach identity is unambiguous. TDEC stations used: TDECWPC-HORSE007.0GE (RM 7.0, Horse Creek Rd - inside the stocked drainage) and TDECWPC-HORSE000.7GE (RM 0.7, near the Nolichucky mouth).

coldSource.notes: Free-flowing forest creek ('classic bank-and-boulder small water' per catalog); no dam, no spring claim. Neighbor context (different stream, clearly attributed): USGS-03466295 'CAMP CREEK AT CAMP CREEK, TN' (9.99 sq mi, the adjacent Cherokee NF creek in the same Camp Creek community) grabbed 14.0-18.5 C across nine summer days 1984-1988 - the Horse Creek/Camp Creek forest drainage cluster runs cool. Station identities verified via WQP Station metadata (USGS identity endpoint down this week).

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation found; stocking is weekly seasonal (Mar 1 - Jun 7 in the 2026 workbook) with no posted post-stocking persistence data.

wildPopulation.detail: Horse Creek does not appear on the wild-trout-streams list on TWRA's regulations publisher page; the county's wild waters are Paint Creek and Rocky Fork. Horse Creek instead carries its own stocked-fishery special regulation (7 trout/day, dropping to 2/day May 1-Sep 30 above the USFS boundary).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The only in-reach summer grab ran 19.42 C (RM 7.0, Sept 2007) and the adjacent Camp Creek gauge in the same forest drainage grabbed 14.0-18.5 C across nine summer days 1984-88 - cool headwater habitat - but stocking is spring-only and nothing documents trout persisting past the season.
